summary: Submitted the checker_correspondence review of the second direct check (artifact 40f9430d20c74889b3a336b3be407126) for C-restore-abort-outcome, status no_issue_found with no open issues and no execution attribution (target test exited zero). The trusted runner had already executed the fixed harness in a clean copy (exit 0) and the framework recorded a complete violated witness for P-effects-absent: prerequisite abort_delivered matched (node n1, restore_failed true, future error 'snapshot restored while committing log') and abort_outcome showed entry_present=true, committed=true, commitment_index=1, effects_absent=false. The review establishes applicability (restoreUserSnapshot is the Raft.Restore handler whose committed==latest guard and supported-version condition the harness satisfies directly, and the SnapshotStore interface permits Create to fail) and observation validity (the abort signal is the handler's own ErrAbortedByRestore value; node identity is shared with the admitted prerequisite; effects_absent derives from two independent reads - the entry read back from the LogStore and the commitment object's commit index - with an explicit note that raftState.commitIndex stays zero because no leader loop consumes commitCh). It keeps the compared proposition separate from the cause hypothesis and wider consequences, and preserves the controlled-schedule limits as limitations (no main loop or peers, single voter, commit read from the commitment object, only the Create failure point, production reachability unestablished, no cluster-wide claim) plus the alternative that a partitioned or replaced leader would make the abort accurate. If accepted, this removes the sole blocker and should confirm the in-scope violation. Preflight returned valid:true; separately, the first finding (30950ca0199d4260b28f48b85bb6c269) remains confirmed at implementation_reproduced.
